reference_materials: Manufacturer-authored 2011 hammer catalogue PDF page 7 and 2022 master catalogue PDF page 60 inspected. Product-family photographs do not identify an exact 56-204 production revision.

Rendered catalogue pages determine visible color/shape; extracted native 2022 JPEG images have different polarity and are not treated as alternate product colors. Source photographs are not redistributed.
findings: All eight final browser captures inspected: complete front/back/top, isolated head front/top/eye, and inferred internal core/bonding front/axial views.
The yellow waisted handle, dark forged head and light machined ends follow the product-family references. Original identification text replaces manufacturer artwork.
The two machined surface domains belong to the same forged head. An actual eye permits inspecting the continuous core and selected bonding-annulus hypothesis.
The 135 mm head and 356 mm overall length are a cross-edition selection. The approximately 49.661 mm steel section and 0.6 mm edge rounding are inferred, not manufacturer dimensions.

The source's 1.8 kg head mass is distinct from the represented approximately 2.027 kg whole tool. A rigid head/handle contact reference contains the inferred mass-centre range with at least 7.57 mm support margin.
An unconstrained CAD handle loft pinched through the core between sections. The final shape-preserving profile retains the jacket, and the visible label conforms to actual mesh facets.
geometry_limits: No official CAD, factory eye/retention dimensions or calibrated surface measurements. Fiberglass, jacket and bonding densities, internal construction and reflectance are inferred.
Static support is not dynamic settling, accepted inertia, a humanoid payload rating or force qualification.
Impact energy, target hardness/compatibility, soil resistance, bond strength, transport and robot operation remain unqualified. Initial inventory and owner acceptance remain open.
